Introduction to Loudoun County Circuit Court

Established in 1757 during Virginia's colonial period, the Loudoun County Circuit Court stands as one of Virginia's primary judicial institutions. Today, it functions as a court of general jurisdiction serving Loudoun County residents, handling a diverse range of civil, criminal, and domestic relations cases.

Current Judiciary

The Loudoun County Circuit Court has four judges who serve eight-year terms after being elected by the Virginia General Assembly:

  • Hon. Jeanette A. Irby
  • Hon. Stephen E. Sincavage
  • Hon. Douglas L. Fleming Jr.
  • Hon. James P. Fisher

Court Jurisdiction and Case Types

Civil Cases

  • Contract disputes
  • Personal injury claims
  • Property litigation
  • Medical malpractice suits
  • Business conflicts
  • Civil appeals from lower courts
  • Cases involving claims exceeding $25,000

Criminal Cases

  • Felony offenses
  • Criminal appeals from General District Court
  • Misdemeanor trials de novo (new trials)
  • Grand jury proceedings
  • Drug trafficking cases
  • Violent crimes
  • White-collar offenses

Family and Domestic Relations

  • Divorce proceedings
  • Property distribution
  • Child custody determinations
  • Spousal and child support
  • Adoption finalization
  • Name changes
  • Marriage license issuance

Other Functions

  • Probate of wills and estate administration
  • Land records and deed registration
  • Appellate review of lower court decisions
  • Issuance of marriage licenses
  • Notary public appointments

Court Procedures

Filing a Case

  1. Prepare appropriate legal documents (available on court website)
  2. Submit documents to the Clerk's Office with required filing fees
  3. Pay applicable filing fees (or request fee waiver if eligible)
  4. Receive case number and initial court date

Typical Case Timeline

  1. Initial Filing: Complaint/petition submitted to clerk's office
  2. Service of Process: Defendant receives copy of complaint/petition
  3. Response Period: Defendant files answer or responsive pleading
  4. Discovery Phase: Parties exchange information and evidence
  5. Pretrial Conferences: Court manages case preparation and settlement discussions
  6. Trial: Evidence and arguments presented before judge or jury
  7. Judgment: Court issues final decision
  8. Appeal Period: Parties have limited time to file appeals

Motions Day Procedures

The court designates specific days for hearing motions (requests for court action):

  • Civil motions: Fridays at 10:00 AM
  • Criminal motions: Fridays at 9:00 AM
  • Emergency motions: May be scheduled as needed
  • Motion filing deadline: Seven calendar days before hearing date

Clerk's Office Services

The Hon. Gary M. Clemens serves as the elected Clerk of the Circuit Court, managing various court functions:

Records Management

Public Services

Courthouse Security

  • Photo identification required
  • Prohibited items include weapons, cameras, and recording devices

Parking Options

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How do I look up case information? A: Case information can be accessed through the Virginia Judiciary's Online Case Information System or by contacting the Clerk's Office directly.

Q: Can I represent myself in Circuit Court? A: Yes, you may represent yourself (pro se), though it's generally advisable to consult with an attorney, especially for complex matters. The court cannot provide legal advice but offers procedural information.

Q: How are jury trials conducted? A: Jury trials involve 7 jurors for civil cases and 12 for criminal cases. Potential jurors are selected from voter and DMV records. Jury duty typically lasts 1-3 days for most trials.

Q: What happens if I miss my court date? A: Missing a criminal court date may result in a capias (arrest warrant). For civil matters, the court may proceed without you or dismiss your case. Contact the court immediately if you miss a scheduled appearance.

Q: How do I appeal a Circuit Court decision? A: Appeals from Circuit Court go to the Virginia Court of Appeals or Supreme Court of Virginia, depending on the case type. Strict filing deadlines apply, typically 30 days from final judgment.

Conclusion

The Loudoun County Circuit Court plays a vital role in Virginia's judicial system, providing a forum for resolving significant legal disputes and administering justice. Understanding its procedures and resources can help litigants navigate the court system more effectively. Whether you're involved in a case or seeking court services, the information above provides a comprehensive overview of this important legal institution.
